items.title: Every window is a proper dialog: focus moves into it and back out, Tab stays inside, Escape and a click beside it close it.
The game's own question window replaces the browser's confirm and prompt boxes.
Notices: short messages at the bottom left that go away by themselves.
Tab rows work as tabs for the keyboard and screen readers.
Buttons that show only a symbol, and search boxes without a label, have names a screen reader can say.
Hints show for the keyboard and on touch screens, not only under a resting mouse.
Cards on the table say what they are and what state they are in.
Mana symbols are read as words.
A "Skip to the table" link, and names for the page's regions.
The focus ring shows everywhere, including on card art.
Play, Edit and View on each recent deck.
A Continue row for what you have begun.
Your ranks on the start menu.
The start menu fits a laptop screen without scrolling.
Draw odds as a chart.
Solo-play results as a chart.
A legend for the matchup grid.
Color sources beside color needs.
The mana curve marks its average and gives the median.
The bracket estimate on a five-step scale.
Print the deck viewer.
The log slides over the table on small screens.
Windows fill the screen on phones.
Notches, home bars and the on-screen keyboard.
Dates and numbers follow the chosen language.
Card pictures decode without holding up the page.
Choose how much a screen reader reads out.
Less background motion.
Easier reading.
A friend's turn clock is announced at 30 and 10 seconds.
Turns of the game log fold.
The stack as cards.
Card art in the game log.
A phase track you can read at a glance.
Click a life total for its history.
One-on-one games use the whole table.
The action bar can be moved off your cards.
The timeline marks where each turn starts.
Graveyard, exile and hand windows can be filtered and put in order.
Your own board is at the bottom of the table.
A clear signal when the game is waiting for you.
Card size on the table.
The card preview waits a moment, and can be docked or turned off.
A full screen button.
Touch preview, and the table's pictures and motion (Phase 2L).
Fill in basic lands.
Search history and kept searches in the deck builder.
Cards without a picture still look like cards.
Legality marks on cards in the deck builder.
Rulings and keyword help in the deck builder's inspector.
Add a whole list of cards at once.
Draw a test hand in the deck builder.
Export from the deck builder.
The deck you are building is kept if you close the builder or the game.
Undo and redo in the deck builder.
Filter and order the deck list.
Keys in the card gallery.
More results load as you scroll.
The setup screen shows its everyday actions and keeps the rest in three menus.
The top bar is shorter: tournaments and history are under More.
A list of every keyboard shortcut.
Menus that work with the keyboard.
A close button in the same place in every window.
Segmented controls.
The theme follows your system until you choose one.
On/off settings in the top bar are switches.
Sliders share one look and say their value.
Bigger touch targets on touch screens.
English-only parts are marked as English for screen readers.
A check that every element the scripts ask for exists.
A stylesheet lint.
The fonts load sooner.
Japanese headings use a matching serif face.
A named scale for what sits on top of what.
